messages:
alex-support: customer reported a sudden surge of long-polling requests to /v1/responses that all end up as 599s. started ~09:20 UTC. SDKs are retrying aggressively and they're seeing double billing. attaching initial logs.
maria-sre: ugh. 599 isn't standard but we've seen it when upstream proxies close while client is still streaming. do we have request ids? can customer share a curl reproducible case?
alex-support: they provided this snippet and logs: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses
```
responses just hang, then client gets HTTP/1.1 599 Connection closed by peer. SDK v0.7.3 auto-retries, which amplifies load. log excerpt: `req_id=ix-7a2e client_ip=3.120.44.2 backend=gw-prod-08 status=599 duration_ms=14503`

lee-eng: thanks. can you paste full gateway logs for `gw-prod-08` around that req_id and also the edge proxy (edge-usw2-3) logs? suspecting slowwrite on the backend or truncated upstream keepalive.
priya-ops: noted. temporarily bumped circuit-breaker to 30s for that customer and disabled automatic SDK retries from server-side (via rate-limiter header override) to stop billing storm. told them to patch SDK to v0.7.4 which includes jittered backoff; customer on older pinned version.
maria-sre: found a cluster of entries where gw-prod-08 reports `write failed: broken pipe` immediately after we forwarded the first chunk. stack shows envoy upstream response reset with `RST_STREAM`. here's snippet: `envoy upstream reset reason=connection termination, response_flag=UH, duration=12ms`

infra-bot: deployment note: node gw-prod-08 was running kernel 5.4.21 with old NIC driver. recent kernel upgrade group fine for others. flagged for upgrade.
lee-eng: if upstream is resetting, the runtime might be closing the connection while kv-cache or prefix streaming still active. need repro that isolates streaming vs non-streaming. alex, can you ask customer to run two tests: 1) single non-streaming generate; 2) streaming with small payloads at 10rps. include tcpdump on client side if possible.
alex-support: asked and customer ran both. non-streaming OK. streaming fails intermittently with same 599 after 12-18s. attached client tcpdump and raw request/response hex shows FIN from our side right after first data chunk.
lee-eng: that matches broken pipe on write. root cause could be a delayed socket close on the node due to epoll timeout bug in our runtime (seen 2024-11 in another cluster). I'll repro locally with a small runtime build that has additional socket tracing. dropping slower connections with zero read after chunk is suspicious.
maria-sre: mitigation plan: 1) cordon gw-prod-08 and shift traffic; 2) push NIC/kernel upgrade and restart runtime; 3) have customer use SDK v0.7.4 and temporary recommend connection keepalive 90s. doing a canary restart now.
priya-ops: sending customer status: "we've identified a node-level network driver issue causing intermittent connection resets for streaming requests. we've shifted your traffic away from the impacted node and are rolling a fix cluster-wide. recommended immediate step: upgrade to SDK v0.7.4 which reduces retry amplification; we'll follow up with timeline for full remediation." want me to post this or tweak wording?
alex-support: post that now, include sticky note about billing: we've credited retry charges incurred during the window. customer asked for ETA on full fix.
maria-sre: ETA: rolling upgrade across production starting in ~20m, expect full completion in 2 hours. will monitor 5xx/599 rate and p95 streaming latencies. raising severity to P1 and paging runtime on-call.
lee-eng: I'll reproduce with a local setup and attach syscall traces. if repro matches, probable fix is small (adjust socket linger/epoll behavior). if not, fallback to adding best-effort write-retry on soft reset.
priya-ops: update: canary node restart succeeded, no 599s for canary traffic over 15m. proceeding cluster-wide. customer update sent. :thumbsup:
alex-support: customer replied: thanks, appreciate the credits and status. will test again from their side after full rollout. closing loop when they verify. :white_check_mark:
